text.title: EU AI Act Compliance — Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules every application of `eu-ai-act-compliance` must enforce — r1-r7 map the system to the Act, r8-r12 govern how an LLM pipeline may produce the documentation. Verifiable at review time; failures gate the artifact.

rule.statement: Classify every AI system risk tier BEFORE any architectural decision; retrofitting compliance costs more than designing for it.
rule.rationale: Risk tier determines which Articles apply, documentation depth, and conformity-assessment path.

rule.statement: Do not deploy any system matching an Article 5 prohibited practice regardless of claimed benefit.
rule.rationale: Article 5 is absolute — no proportionality test. Fines EUR 35M or 7% global turnover. Effective Feb 2025.

rule.statement: If the system maps to Annex III, treat as high-risk and apply Articles 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 43.
rule.rationale: Annex III enumerates 8 domains where AI decisions affect fundamental rights. High-risk obligations apply Aug 2026.

rule.statement: For chatbots, synthetic-content generators, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation: disclose AI involvement clearly and at the earliest opportunity.
rule.rationale: Article 50 requires transparency where users may assume human interaction or be misled.

rule.statement: GPAI providers MUST publish a model card + training-data summary; >10^25 FLOPs models MUST also red-team and report serious incidents.
rule.rationale: Systemic-risk threshold targets foundation models with broad societal impact. Enforcement active Aug 2026.

rule.statement: Every high-risk system MUST provide effective human-oversight controls (override, stop, audit log) per Article 14.
rule.rationale: Automated rejection with no override path violates Article 14 — design constraint, not a UI add-on.

rule.statement: Every requirement in a compliance draft MUST cite the specific Article / Annex number.

rationale.source: EU AI Act drafting practice; Kennedys Law 2026

rule.rationale: Articles are the contract. Vague compliance prose is unauditable.

rule.statement: Every Act-article citation in generated content MUST be validated against the official Act text on eur-lex.europa.eu before the document leaves the pipeline. Syntactic pattern-matching alone does not satisfy this — a well-formed citation to a non-existent article still fails.
rule.rationale: LLMs interpolate plausible-looking article numbers from training data; a regulator who spots one fabricated citation discounts the whole submission, including the parts that were correct.

rule.statement: No compliance document produced by the agent MAY be submitted to a regulator without explicit sign-off from a named human with legal competence. The orchestrator halts; it does not proceed on a timeout.
rule.rationale: The Act treats submitted documentation as legally binding, so un-reviewed agent output is a self-inflicted breach rather than a draft.

rule.statement: All compliance artefacts — model cards, bias reports, data lineage, conformity assessments — MUST live in version-controlled storage with immutable history.
rule.rationale: Article 11 documentation must be reconstructible as it stood at any past date; a mutable share drive cannot answer what was claimed when.

rule.statement: CI MUST re-trigger classification whenever a feature, training-data scope, or deployment context changes. The risk tier is not static.
rule.rationale: Adding biometric authentication to a limited-risk recommender flips it to high-risk; without the trigger the documentation lags reality and the system operates illegally in the gap.

rule.statement: If the compliance pipeline itself processes personal data — bias checks over real user records, for example — GDPR data-subject rights MUST be honoured independently: DPIA, legal basis, retention window.
rule.rationale: GDPR applies independently of the Act, so ignoring it while doing Act work creates a second, distinct violation out of the remediation itself.
